questions.question: When driving under a bridge or overpass, what should you do?

options.text: Trust that the posted clearance height is correct.
Do not assume the posted clearance height is correct.
Measure the height of the opening before driving under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the posted clearance height is correct.
questions.explanation: Posted height clearances may not be accurate. The road may have been repaved after the sign was posted, or snow on the ground may reduce the actual clearance. If you are not sure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal on a vehicle with air brakes:

options.text: Is not recommended.
Is required.
Is optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle parked, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake.
Use the parking brake only if parked on a hill.
Do not use the parking brake because it can damage the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing outside.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Rarely happens to large trucks.
Usually happens when driving faster than 65 mph.
Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a large amount of water for this to happen.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: An impaired driver.
A color-blind driver.
A driver who does not know traffic rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: An impaired driver.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One sign of impairment is stopping at inappropriate places, like at green traffic lights.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the flames.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stand as far away from the fire as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not at the flames. If you are unsure what type of extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous material fire, wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
Not use wheel chocks.
Use wheel chocks only after using the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parking on a level surface. If your vehicle does not have spring brakes, wheel chocks are essential to prevent it from moving.

questions.question: When you start an engine:

options.text: The brakes will lock up.
Warning lights should turn on, then turn off quickly.
Coolant temperature should drop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should stop after a few seconds. If they do not turn off, there may be a problem with the vehicle.

questions.question: Vehicles with low underneath clearance are difficult to drive:

options.text: Over railroad crossings.
In rural areas.
On wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be hard to cross when pulling a trailer with low clearance. Specially low-slung units and single-axle tractors with long trailers are very difficult to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It fills the tires.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system. The air compressor governor controls the compressor.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle than yours can usually:

options.text: Stop faster than your vehicle.
Take longer to stop than your vehicle.
Stop in about the same time as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far back to follow other vehicles.

questions.question: If other vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a multi-lane road, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Drive on the shoulder.
Stay in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your truck is slow due to a heavy load. This lets other vehicles pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: When crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for you.
Wait for a large enough gap to cross safely.
Rely only on your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap to cross safely.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. Always wait for a large enough gap in traffic to cross safely.

questions.question: Class 1 hazardous material is:

options.text: An explosive.
A liquid.
Corrosive.

questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Explosives are Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, you should:

options.text: Never drive faster than the posted limit.
May exceed it when passing another vehicle.
May exceed it in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never drive faster than the posted limit.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must slow down based on road and weather conditions. You should never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: The ____ trailer is most likely to roll over if you turn too quickly.

options.text: Front
Last
Middle

questions.correctAnswerText: Last
questions.explanation: Make turns slowly and smoothly when pulling trailers. Quick turns can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use only one set of turn signals.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Always use your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the road. This is very important at night.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, you should shift to a lower gear:

options.text: Before you start the hill.
After you have already started the hill.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the hill.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before starting a downhill grade. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster going downhill.

questions.question: Before a trip, the glide plate should be:

options.text: Detached from the vehicle.
Far from the upper fifth wheel.
Securely attached to the trailer frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Securely attached to the trailer frame.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough inspection before every trip. The glide plate must be securely attached to the trailer frame.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Work properly.
Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.
Allow better acceleration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes will wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.
